title: Independent transactional verification capacity slots

requirements.QSL01: Remove the globally exclusive queue counter from ordinary admission and completion.
requirements.QSL02: Retain the exact configured combined queue bound, eight pending jobs per player, fairness, immutable retries and leases.
requirements.QSL03: Preserve existing pending jobs and their metadata through a coordinated migration.
requirements.QSL04: Reproduce the old blocking behavior and verify the fix with real PostgreSQL transactions.

implementation.admission: A pending race, publication or legacy validation owns one queue_reservations row with a unique slot in the configured range. PostgreSQL probes available slots using per-slot transaction-scoped nonblocking advisory locks; the unique slot constraint is the final capacity fence. Slots are acquired in the job's own transaction, never an external queue or process-memory cache.
implementation.completion: Terminal transitions and pending-job deletion remove only that job's reservation and update only its owner's pending counter. There is no write to a global queue total. Claiming and infrastructure retries retain the same reservation; terminal explicit retry reacquires capacity.
implementation.rollback: Admission failure or process/transaction rollback cannot leave a committed reservation behind. An uncommitted release remains occupied to other transactions until commit, so it cannot be counted as spare capacity prematurely. Rolling back a completion restores its reservation.
implementation.owner_fairness: QueuePlayer still owns the exact pending count and last-claim timestamp. Admission locks that owner's row and preserves the eight-job limit; claim ordering is unchanged.
implementation.configuration: Ordinary admissions take mutually compatible shared reads of queue_limits; these do not serialize admissions. Only capacity changes take an exclusive configuration lock. A reduction that would leave an occupied slot outside the new range fails closed with QUEUE_CAPACITY_CHANGE_REQUIRES_DRAIN. Replicas must use the same capacity setting.
implementation.read_compatibility: queue_capacity is now a read-only aggregate view over reservations. Existing queue-depth diagnostics and the load lab retain exact reads without a shared counter write.
implementation.pressure: If concurrent uncommitted admissions occupy every slot, the database rejects another admission immediately with its fixed verification_capacity_reached error. The API maps only that precise PostgreSQL/SQLite error to HTTP 429 without treating it as a dependency outage. A saved upload/key can retry normally.
implementation.bounded_cost: Free-slot search is bounded by configured queue capacity; the exact depth read scans only live reservations, not players or historical runs. This replaces global serialization, not every possible queue/database cost. Current default capacity is 128. SQLite retains its inherent single-writer behavior and uses equivalent transactional slot constraints.

migration.integration: The migration joins independently prepared concurrent reward and Studio branches into one head. It changes only queue tables/triggers; it does not implement, undo or claim those other tasks.
migration.backfill: A bounded active-job union allocates one slot per queued/verifying race or publication and queued/validating legacy validation. The old total must match reconstructed pending jobs or migration stops for investigation. Only active owners' pending rows are upserted; there is no update of every account. Last-claim timestamps and all original job columns are retained.
migration.initial_limit: The migration seeds at least the existing 128 default slots of capacity, or enough capacity for the complete original backlog. Runtime configuration may increase this; reducing the occupied slot range can require a drain.
migration.rollback: The downgrade reconstructs the historical total and triggers without changing job records. The focused test exercises downgrade/upgrade twice with active leases, compares all job columns and retains the original last-claim timestamp. Because the migration joins branches, use explicit revision targets rather than an ambiguous relative -1.
activation: Take the normal reviewed database/object backup and quiesce API writers and all worker roles.
Apply the complete reviewed migration head, then start matching API and worker artifacts with one consistent BMT_MAX_QUEUED_RUNS setting.
Verify queue depth, owner counts, exact duplicate receipts and leased-job recovery before reopening traffic.
Do not mix old counter-writing workers/APIs with the new read-only queue_capacity view.

validation.original_behavior: Saved original queueing.py plus original counter triggers reproduce four real PostgreSQL lock timeouts: a held race or publication completion blocks another owner's admission and completion. original-linux.xml/log retain the actual failures. The isolated baseline copy omits the slot migration and does not use a live service.
covered: An unrelated admission and terminal completion commit while a race or publication completion remains uncommitted.
Sixteen simultaneous submissions preserve a four-job shared cap, and concurrent submissions for one owner preserve the eight-job bound.
An uncommitted admission prevents oversubscription; an actual HTTP upload receives 429, then succeeds under the same key after rollback and returns the same receipt on repetition.
Queued-to-verifying/validating-to-queued transitions retain capacity; terminal transitions, explicit retry, deletion and rollback keep exact counters for all three job kinds.
An old terminal job cannot release a slot already reused by another job.
Capacity increases remain safe; unsafe reductions reject without losing jobs; drained queues can safely shrink.
Migration preserves all queued job columns, leased ownership metadata and fairness timestamps across repeated upgrade/downgrade.
